target:
def Target : Prop :=
  ∀ (Fm S₀ S : Type) [LogicalConnective Fm] [LogicalNeutral Fm] [Entailment S₀ Fm] [Entailment S Fm]
    (𝓑 : S₀) (𝓢 : S) [Entailment.Cl 𝓑] [Entailment.Cl 𝓢] (K F : Fm → Fm),
    Def1 𝓑 K → 𝓑 ⪯ 𝓢 → Def2 𝓢 K → Def4 𝓢 K →
    Def5 𝓑 F →
    (∀ φ, 𝓢 ⊢ K (K φ 🡒 F φ)) →
    ∃ ψ, 𝓢 ⊢ K ψ ⋏ K (∼F ψ)

divergences.description: The implication in hypothesis (ii) is reversed. The source states case (ii) of Theorem 1 as T ⊢ B(F[p] → Bp) (every sentence in F is knowable / F is 'safe'), whereas Target assumes ∀ φ, 𝓢 ⊢ K (K φ 🡒 F φ) (every knowable sentence is in F). This materially changes the claim and renders Target mathematically false: for instance, taking 𝓑 = 𝓢 to be propositional modal logic S4 with K = □ and F φ = ⊤ satisfies all six hypotheses (with ψ = ⊥ witnessing Def5 𝓑 F, and □φ 🡒 ⊤ being a tautology), yet S4 does not prove □ψ ⋏ □(∼⊤).

First-order arithmetic, Robinson arithmetic Q, Gödel numbering, quantifiers, and F being a formula with one free variable applied to sentence codes are not modelled; Target instead abstracts sentences to an arbitrary type Fm, takes K and F to be arbitrary functions Fm → Fm, and assumes the Gödel fixed point directly via Def5 𝓑 F (∃ ψ, 𝓑 ⊢ ψ 🡘 ∼F ψ) rather than deriving it from T including Q. (This abstraction is acknowledged in the author's claim.)

Def1 𝓑 K assumes full closure of the base system 𝓑 under the necessitation rule (∀ φ, 𝓑 ⊢ φ → 𝓑 ⊢ K φ, yielding arbitrarily nested applications of K), whereas Reinhardt's proof remark in P-R324 notes that only a single B-prefix on tautologies and the elementary axioms of arithmetic and equality is needed (though full necessitation for the base system follows in the full background system of P-R323 with Bp → BBp).

judgement.summary: Target is divergent from case (ii) of Reinhardt's Theorem 1 because it reverses the implication in hypothesis (ii) from F[p] → Bp to K φ 🡒 F φ, changing the meaning from soundness/safety of F to completeness of F and making the formalized proposition false. Aside from this major error, the formalization matches the abstract structure of the theorem with only minor idealizations (abstracting away arithmetic, Q, and Gödel numbering via an explicit fixed-point hypothesis, and assuming full necessitation on the base system).
